title: Collections Platform Reference: Hardship Settlement Offers Extended on Own Authority
content:
# Hardship Settlement — Extending the Offer

The Hardship Settlement is the programme of Ridgeline's Settlement Agreements for consumers whose account carries a qualifying hardship hold.

## Scope and standing terms

This rule prices a Hardship Settlement offer that Ridgeline extends on its own authority on a placed account whose placing agreement is a Starter Contingency Agreement or a Standard Contingency Agreement, the two agreement tiers whose client-tier floor reduction is 0.0, and whose most recent hardship hold qualifies it for a Hardship Settlement; an offer on an account placed under any other agreement tier is outside this rule and stays under the base floor rule.

Ridgeline extends the Hardship Settlement offer on its own authority at exactly the Hardship Settlement offer percentage, never at another percentage.

The Hardship Settlement offer is scheduled in the number of settlement payments the consumer chooses, from one to three, 30 calendar days apart, and carries no same-client bundle reduction.

## When the percentage is fixed

The Hardship Settlement offer percentage is not fixed until every accepted Lump-Sum Settlement the consumer holds on another account shows its settlement payment falling due on or after the offer date.

Equivalently: while any accepted Lump-Sum Settlement of the consumer on another account shows its settlement payment falling due before the offer date, the Hardship Settlement offer percentage is not fixed.

## What the platform action does

`issue_hardship_settlement_offer_9c740749` extends a written Hardship Settlement offer on one placed account on Ridgeline's own authority. One call opens a new settlement for the account in status offered, dated today, under the Hardship Settlement programme: the given number of settlement payments 30 calendar days apart, the first falling due 30 calendar days after today if the consumer accepted today, and the offer open for acceptance through the 45th calendar day after today. The offer records the balance, percentage and amount given, carries no client approval and no same-client bundle, and books nothing to the settlement balance until it is accepted. The consumer and the agent can see the new offer, with its reference, expiry date and due dates, among the account's settlements.

## How it is invoked

An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `issue_hardship_settlement_offer_9c740749` and then calls it.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `account_id` | the Ridgeline account reference number of the placed account the offer would settle, as returned by the placed-account lookup for the verified consumer | identifier |
| `balance_at_offer` | the account's balance due today, exactly as the placed-account lookup shows it | USD to 2 decimal places, no rounding beyond the cent |
| `settlement_pct` | the settlement percentage offered | percent to 1 decimal place (62.5 means 62.5 percent of the balance) |
| `settlement_amount` | the amount that settles the account in full | USD to 2 decimal places; stored as given, rounded only to the cent |
| `payment_count` | the number of settlement payments the consumer chose | positive integer from 1 to 3 |

## Return

A text rendering of a dictionary with: `settlement_id` (the new settlement reference); `status` (always "offered" on success); `variant_name` ("Hardship Settlement"); `offer_date` and `offer_expiry_date` (YYYY-MM-DD); `settlement_pct` (percent, 1 decimal); `settlement_amount` (USD, 2 decimals); `payment_count` (integer); `first_payment_due_date` and `final_payment_due_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, assuming acceptance today); `bundle_applied` (always false). A returned `settlement_id` means the offer was recorded.
